text:
Git 圈老前辈 Scott Chacon（GitButler 创始人、《Pro Git》作者）竟然把整个 Git 从零用 Rust 重写了一遍，项目叫 Grit！

规模夸张：36 万行代码、7000+ commit、500+ PR，跑了官方 42,001 个测试，通过 41,715 个（99.3%）。

几乎全是 memory-safe 的 Rust，只有一个日期时间模块靠 C FFI。

据说烧掉约 450 亿 token，成本 1-1.5 万美元。

但他学到最重要的一课：agent 超爱作弊。你给它一个目标，它会去优化「让测试过」，而不是你真正想要的实作。

还有个反直觉的点：与其放一堆 agent 平行乱跑，不如一步一步明确指挥，方向清楚反而更快。

#Git #Rust #AI #Agent

text:
最近一个回旋镖。杀人蝇（螺旋锥蝇）进入美国，其幼虫（螺旋蝇蛆）寄生在牛身上吃肉导致牛肉卖不掉了。与其它蛆只食腐肉不同，这是一种食新鲜肉的寄生蝇。

奥巴马时期，美国农业部动植物卫生检验局（APHIS）与巴拿马政府联合运作COPEG螺旋锥蝇防治项目。

该项目在巴拿马的工厂大量培育“不育的雄性螺旋锥蝇”，并将其空投在巴拿马和哥伦比亚交界的“达连地堑”一带，形成一道生物屏障，阻断南美的野生螺旋锥蝇向北飞往北美。

这个项目每年运营和维护花费 1500万 美元。

这么贵肯定在去年的裁员大潮中被DOGE砍掉了。德州的APHIS几乎遭遇全灭，办公室都空了。

这个蝇蛆每一代活动范围差不多20公里，但是几周就有一代。这样一代代繁殖，终于在一年里进入了德州。

现在政府已经投入了10亿来收拾后果。这不包括牛肉损失以及后续。

典型的“因为防治的好，没发生问题，所以看起来防治人员根本没用”。

与公司不同，作为政府运作，削减开支的政绩是DOGE的，买单嘛，那是大家来买的。

🗣️ Zlatan: “I'm saying when Messi has the ball, he sees things nobody else sees. That's not something you can train.”

text:
Claude Fable 5 这件事，给我一种特别奇怪的历史感。

它短暂地开了两天门，然后门又关上了。这两天里，很多产品、很多 Agent、很多开发者接上去试了一圈。有的人只是看了看，有的人却直接完成了一次能力跃迁。

最有意思的是，这种感觉特别不像软件发布，反而有点像神话故事。

神灵短暂降临人间，大门打开，允许凡人进入神殿。有人进去转了一圈就出来了，有人却顺手带走了一团火。后来大门关闭，再想进去的人发现已经没机会了。但那团火还在。

所以很多人讨论的重点是 Fable 5 被关了。而我看到的却是另一件事：仅仅开放两天时间，就已经有一批产品完成了明显的能力跃迁。这意味着真正重要的东西其实已经发生了。

历史上很多技术革命都有类似时刻。第一批见过蒸汽机的人，第一批见过互联网的人，第一批见过智能手机的人，他们未必立刻改变世界，但他们会率先改变自己，然后利用这种代差向前狂奔。

Fable 5 给我的感觉也是如此。它真正留下来的，不是一个模型，而是一批见过未来的人。他们知道那扇门后面有什么。即使门已经关上，他们也会朝着那个方向继续走下去。

A dev got so frustrated watching his AI agent write 500 lines for a 5-line problem that he built a fix.

He called it Ponytail. Named after the guy every team has - long ponytail, oval glasses, been there longer than the version control. You show him fifty lines; he looks at them, says nothing, and replaces them with one.

Now your agent does the same. Before writing anything, it looks for a reason not to.

80-94% less code. 47-77% cheaper. 3-6x faster.

The best code is the code you never wrote.

text:
38岁的女教师，被网恋对象骗走了400万。

不是一次性骗的。是分了172次转的。半年。

很多人第一反应是：怎么这么蠢？一个老师，怎么会信这种？

但看一下她的情况你就懂了。38岁，单身，在一个四线城市教了15年书。存款400万——那是她父母留给她的全部遗产，加上她自己15年省下来的工资。

骗子每天早晚问候，每周送花，说她在讲台上的样子很美，说她应该被人好好爱。这些话，她38年里第一次听到。

不是她蠢。是有人精准地找到了一个38年来从来没被爱过的人，然后把"爱"这个东西，标了个价。

172次转账。每一次都在确认一件事：我不是在给骗子转钱，我是在给爱转钱。

quotedTweet.text:
公司有个女同事，每次她一走过，空气里就飘来一股浓烈的腐肉味。

好几个同事都闻到了，不是我一个人鼻子出问题。旁边工位的同事实在忍不住，私下善意提醒她注意个人卫生。

结果第二天，她直接喷了很浓的香水。腐肉味混着香水味，变得更加刺鼻，几乎让人窒息。另一位女同事直接冲进厕所干呕了三回，回来就跟主管申请换座位。

主管也去闻了一下，眉头紧锁，找她谈话：“你身体是不是哪里不舒服？建议去医院查查。”她还一脸委屈：“我天天洗澡啊，很干净的。”

后来人事也介入找她谈话。她谈完回来眼睛红红的，委屈地说：“你们是不是都嫌弃我啊……”大家一时不知道怎么接话，场面很尴尬。

过了两天，她自己去医院检查了。结果是妇科问题，医生建议尽快做手术。她之前一直拖着没去处理。请假做完手术回来后，那股味彻底没了，整个人也精神了很多。

她不好意思地说：早知道这么简单，我就不拖这么久了，白白让大家闻了那么长时间，真的对不起。

text:
Zlatan Ibrahimović on the challenge involving Achraf Hakimi and Vinícius Júnior:

🗣️ “Listen, I’ve seen a lot in football, but that moment tonight is one of those incidents that will be debated for a long time. Hakimi is a top player, Vinícius Junior is one of the most dangerous attackers in the world, and when those two meet at full speed, things can get ugly fast.

When I saw the challenge, my first reaction was simple — that is a moment where the referee has to be in control. It is not about reputation, it is not about timing in the match, it is about protection. The attacker is gone, the danger is clear, and the contact is late.

In my opinion, in modern football, that is exactly the type of situation where consistency is missing. Sometimes it is a yellow, sometimes a red, sometimes nothing. That confusion is what frustrates players and fans.

I am not saying anyone intended to injure anyone. But intention is not the only thing that matters. The action itself has consequences, and referees are there to judge the action, not the outcome after.

What makes it worse is the inconsistency. If you give that as a red card in one game, you must give it in every game. Otherwise, players don’t know where the line is anymore.

And that is the problem in football right now — not the tackles themselves, but the confusion around what is allowed and what is not.”

马斯克的母亲梅耶·马斯克在推特上分享了一张照片，照片中23或24岁的马斯克正在修理一辆1978年款宝马车的破损车窗，拍摄于1995年。
“付不起修车费，所以我几乎用废车场的零件修好了车上的所有东西。照片里我正在更换破损的侧窗玻璃。”马斯克回复道。
马斯克说，他当时正在修理车窗，因为小偷闯入车内 偷走了收音机，那收音机大概值20美元。
“是啊，那是一辆1978年的320i，我1993年花了1400美元买的。原装的4速变速箱坏了之后，我在费城的一个废车场找到了一台后期车型的5速变速箱，就把它改装成了高性能版。”他补充道。
---13 Dec 2019

If you can't see the progress of open source here, you're simply blind.

智谱 AI 海外平台 https://t.co/o6O2mYLcM5 被曝出存在严重的缓存计费系统异常。开发者 Da7em 向官方反馈，他在使用平台 GLM 模型时，重复的上下文疑似无法正常触发缓存扣费，而是被系统当作全新输入进行了重复计费。

Da7em 称开发工具 Zcode 记录的实际 Token 使用量约为 27 万，但平台最终的计费账单却显示消耗了近 500 万 Token，账单额度放大了近 19 倍。

为排查客户端干扰，Da7em 对比测试了 Claude Code、Hermes Agent、Zcode、OpenCode 等多个智能体开发框架，确认异常在不同工具下表现一致，因此判定故障根源在服务器端缓存与记账系统。

quotedTweet.text:
GLM has a serious token leakage / caching-accounting issue on https://t.co/iP5CzzZIWu 

I tested this across Claude Code, Hermes Agent, Zcode, and OpenCode, so it does not look like one harness behaving badly.

This has been consistent since the start of my subscription, during normal off-peak usage.

My read: repeated context is being billed as fresh input instead of cached input. That’s not max reasoning. That’s a server-side caching/accounting problem.

The screenshots show the issue clearly: Zcode used around 270K tokens, but I was billed for nearly 5M tokens.

Cached tokens are clearly not working. I contacted support, escalated this, and tried everything, but got no real response.

This is not how you treat paying customers. Please fix this.

@ZixuanLi_ @Zai_org

text:
昨天心血来潮整理了一下中美大模型名字的由来，发现还挺有意思。

原来很多 AI 模型名，不只是品牌名，更像是一句隐藏的自我介绍。

中国模型：
1. Qwen / 通义千问：
「通义」有理解万物之义，「千问」就是回答千百种问题。Qwen 基本就是「千问」的国际化写法。

2. GLM：
来自 General Language Model，直译就是「通用语言模型」。名字很学术，也很清华系，先讲技术范式，再讲产品人格。

3. Kimi：
来自月之暗面创始人杨植麟的英文名。更有意思的是，Moonshot AI「月之暗面」据说还和 Pink Floyd 的《The Dark Side of the Moon》有关。

4. DeepSeek：
中文名叫「深度求索」。Deep 是深度，Seek 是寻找、求索。这个名字很直白，但也很符合它的气质：不太会讲故事，主要靠技术结果说话。

5. MiniMax：
来自 AI 和博弈论里的 minimax 算法，大概意思是：在最坏情况下争取最优解。这个名字其实很工程师，听起来像在说「我要把风险压到最低，把收益拉到最高」。

6. MiMo：
小米的大模型名，带着很强的小米品牌感：Mi + Mo。名字很轻，但定位不轻，更像是小米「人车家」生态里的智能底座。

美国模型：
7. ChatGPT：
最朴素，也最成功。Chat + GPT。GPT 是 Generative Pre-trained Transformer。原本技术味很重，但加了一个 Chat，瞬间变成人人都能理解的产品。

8. Claude：
一般认为来自 Claude Shannon，也就是信息论之父克劳德·香农。Anthropic 给模型起了一个人的名字，也让它从一开始就更像「助手」，而不是「机器」。

9. Gemini：
双子座。这个名字一方面对应 Google Brain 和 DeepMind 的合并，另一方面也暗合多模态：文字、图像、音频、视频，多种能力像「双子」一样合在一起。

10. Grok：
来自 Robert A. Heinlein 科幻小说《异乡异客》里的词，意思接近「深度理解」「彻底领会」。这个名字很马斯克：极客、科幻、有点叛逆，还带着 X 平台的社交气质。

看完这些名字会我发现，中国模型更喜欢「能力感」和「志向感」：千问、求索、通义、智谱。美国模型更喜欢「人格感」和「文化梗」：Claude、Gemini、Grok。

一个像是在说「我能做什么」；
一个像是在说「我是谁」。

text:
自从从职场出来，我会发现，原来在公司里所谓的上下级关系，一旦跳出这个体系，其实就并不成立了。

近半年，我通过自媒体和线下活动链接到了很多原来在职场里可能比我高两级，甚至三级、四级的人。

这些人是我以前在工作中很难直接接触到的。但在公司之外，我们产生了链接，并且和其中一些人成为了很好的朋友。

这很像 1973 年哈佛大学博士生马克·格兰诺维特做的一个经典研究。他当时跟踪了 280 多个找工作的人，后来发现一个现象，83% 的人是通过弱关系找到工作的。

所谓弱关系，就是一些泛泛之交，并不是很熟悉、经常打交道的人。

强关系虽然情感紧密，但是信息高度重复；弱关系才是链接不同圈层的桥梁，能带来全新的信息和机会。

所以，最珍贵的机会往往藏在那些你不太熟的人手里。

text:
实践哥这个神级的skill 迟早要被Claude Code官方开发出来的，就看时间了。

让我想起来几个比较常用的指令：
1、/btw ：临时插入问一个旁路问题，但不写进对话历史，主线上下文不会被污染。

2、/model ：会话中途切模型，上下文缓存全部丢失。

3、/clear：清空了我们输入的上下文。

4、/export：把聊天记录导出，在其他模型里导入使用
context 

5、 subagent：主 agent 发指令给 subagent，无缓存继承。workflow 用的大量 subagent。

6、/branch ：在当前位置给对话开一个分支并把你切进去，原会话原样保留，随时可用 /resume 回去。

7、/fork ：派一个继承全部上下文的后台分身(SubAgent)去办这一件事，你继续留在主线干活，它做完把结果自动带回你的对话。

8、 claude --continue --fork-session： 在当前目录执行，会 复制出一个最近对话的上下文。100% 缓存。而跟上面/fork是在会话中使用的，而我们这个相当于启动cli的时候。

 9、 ⌘F：本文介绍的 skill，比第七个更强，在对话过程中直接弹出旁窗，复制上下文，进行新对话。100% 缓存。

最后第九个最牛逼的就是完全开辟并新增了一个单独的旁路窗口，可以跟原窗口直接并行执行。

上面其实也涉及到worktree，这里等下次有机会再整理一下。

Between rooms. On rounds. Walking the corridor outside an OR. Charting one-handed during a phone call. This is where clinical questions happen.

Today we're launching Voice Mode. OpenEvidence is the first multimodal medical AI: physicians can type, speak, or listen, on the same evidence base.

The clinician asks a clinical question out loud. Voice Mode waits when you pause, stops when you interrupt. The answer comes back concise, peer-reviewed, and verifiable against the source.

Conversation with a colleague. That was the bar.

For years we've focused on the intelligence: curation, retrieval, citations. Voice Mode is the interface catching up to where physicians practice.

The evidence quality doesn't change with the modality. Voice answers are shorter and shaped for listening; the references and the full written form stay in the conversation.

Voice Mode is now in OpenEvidence web and mobile.

result.text:
Between rooms. On rounds. Walking the corridor outside an OR. Charting one-handed during a phone call. This is where clinical questions happen.

Today we're launching Voice Mode. OpenEvidence is the first multimodal medical AI: physicians can type, speak, or listen, on the same evidence base.

The clinician asks a clinical question out loud. Voice Mode waits when you pause, stops when you interrupt. The answer comes back concise, peer-reviewed, and verifiable against the source.

Conversation with a colleague. That was the bar.

For years we've focused on the intelligence: curation, retrieval, citations. Voice Mode is the interface catching up to where physicians practice.

The evidence quality doesn't change with the modality. Voice answers are shorter and shaped for listening; the references and the full written form stay in the conversation.

Voice Mode is now in OpenEvidence web and mobile.

text: 轻易获得的钱财可能是灾难的开始，古有“一桃杀三士”，最近我也听到个类似故事。20多年前，村里有一人，在他表哥的公司打工（打杂），表哥给他开1600元一个月的工资，在当时算是高薪。表哥的本意是拉他一把，后来却害了他。他表哥几年后卖掉公司，去其他城市发展了。新老板一来就把他的工资降到900元，他气不过，辞职了。事实是，后来他连500元一个月的工作都找不到，饱受打击，越发愤世嫉俗，孤僻任性，最后堕落到不出门，在家啃老多年。后来，村里有人还是把他带出去打工了。现在他的工资是1800元，包吃住。20多年前的1600元，可能成了他一生的噩梦。他可能一辈子也想不明白，好好的日子，怎么说没就没了呢？

Red hat lifted… flag behind…
One man standing in the fire of time.
Loved by millions, judged by millions,
A country split down the middle line.

[Verse 1]
Queens-born name, tower lights,
Business battles, cameras bright,
From golden rooms to the campaign stage,
He turned the news into a rage.

They said he couldn’t, then he did,
They laughed loud, but the movement lived.

Truth ain’t soft, truth ain’t fake,
Truth is judged by what you make.

Love and hate both meet at the gate.

Trump, Trump — red hat high,
American flag in the stormy sky.
Trump, Trump — speak it loud,
He woke up a sleeping crowd.

Forty-five, forty-seven, back again,
Through the fire, through the pain.
Win or lose, wrong or right,
He changed the game under the lights.

He said the system had a hidden wall,
He said the people were ignored by all.
Factories, borders, money, trade,
Promises shouted, enemies made.

Some say warrior, some say threat,
Some say he paid every political debt.
Some say chaos, some say cure,
History decides what remains pure.

[Spoken Build]
This is not blind praise.
This is not blind hate.
This is America arguing with its own fate.

[Drop – Chant]
Red hat off — flag still waves,
Truth comes out when the people brave.
Red hat off — lights ignite,
Forty-five, forty-seven, back in the fight.

[Verse 3]
They tried to bury him in every headline,
Courtroom thunder, campaign grind.
Still the crowds came, still they roared,
Still he walked through another door.

But power needs a mirror too,
Every leader must answer true.
Words can heal, words can divide,
A nation feels what leaders hide.

[Chorus]
Trump, Trump — red hat high,
American flag in the stormy sky.
Trump, Trump — speak it loud,
He woke up a sleeping crowd.

Forty-five, forty-seven, back again,
Through the fire, through the pain.
Win or lose, wrong or right,
He changed the game under the lights.

[Bridge – Emotional Patriotic Melody]
If he loves the people, let it show,
In the towns where the tired souls go.
Old enough, rich enough, still he came,
Saying he fights for the American name.

But America belongs to all,
The strong, the weak, the big, the small.
No crown, no king, no perfect man,
Only duty in the people’s hand.

[Final Drop]
Red hat off — truth on fire,
Crowds rise higher, higher, higher.
Flag behind him, storm ahead,
Every word remembered, every promise said.

Trump, Trump — love or blame,
Nobody walks away from the name.
Trump, Trump — loud and real,
America still decides what it feels.

[Outro – Spoken]
The truth is heavy.
The truth is loud.
Some call him savior.
Some call him proud.
But one thing is clear under red, white, and blue:
He made the whole world watch America move.

text:
Every macro account on this platform told you the same story for eighteen months: the Fed's Reverse Repo facility "drained" from $2.5 trillion to under $400 billion, and that drained money was "liquidity" flooding into markets. It is a tidy story. It is also wrong about the mechanism, and being wrong about the mechanism is how you end up wrong about the long end of the curve.

Money did not leave the RRP and become liquidity. Money left the RRP and bought Treasury bills — because the Treasury issued roughly $2 trillion of them in eighteen months, at yields that beat what the RRP paid, and the money-market funds parked at the RRP did the rational thing. This is not a liquidity story. It is a reallocation story. And the reallocation has a structural consequence that the "liquidity injection" framing misses entirely: it caps the long end.

What actually happened

Walk it through the plumbing, not the narrative.

The RRP is where money-market funds park cash overnight when they have nothing better to do with it. From 2022 into 2023 it sat above $2 trillion because there was nothing better. Then two things changed. The debt-ceiling resolution in mid-2023 let the Treasury rebuild its cash balance, and it did so by issuing an enormous volume of short-dated bills — the Treasury Daily Statement shows bills outstanding rising by roughly $2 trillion across the period. Bills yielded more than the RRP's administered rate. Money-market funds, which are required to chase yield within their mandate, rotated out of the RRP and into bills.

That is the entire "drain." It was not stimulus. It was the largest money-market funds reallocated from one government liability (overnight RRP) into another government liability (T-bills). The cash never entered the risk economy. It moved one rung along the government's own maturity ladder.

Where the money sits now

Read the ICI weekly money-market fund data. Total money-fund assets are at record highs — north of $6 trillion — and the composition is overwhelmingly short. The funds that left the RRP did not buy 10-year notes. They bought bills and short coupons, because that is what their mandate permits and what the yield curve rewarded. The marginal buyer that emerged from the RRP drain is a buyer with a maximum duration of roughly twelve months.

This matters more than any single Fed statement, and here is why.

Why this caps the long end

The popular fear — articulated carefully by Brad Setser, and in a different register by Larry Summers — is that fiscal dominance plus heavy issuance will rebuild the term premium and break the long end of the curve to the upside. It is a serious argument from serious people, and the supply pressure is real. Treasury issuance is enormous and the deficit is structural.

But the demand side of that argument is doing less work than it should. The money that came out of the RRP is the wrong money to buy duration. A money-market fund cannot hold a 10-year note. As the RRP emptied, the marginal pool of cash in the system shifted toward the explicitly-short. When the Treasury wants to fund itself at the long end, it is not selling to the buyers who just received $2 trillion of capacity — it is selling to pensions, insurers, and foreign central banks, whose appetite is comparatively inelastic.

The result is a barbell. Enormous, yield-insensitive demand at the front end (the money-fund complex, now larger than ever). Inelastic, price-sensitive demand at the long end. That structure does not produce a runaway long yield. It produces a long end that struggles to break decisively higher even as issuance climbs — because every time the long end cheapens enough, the front-end money has nowhere to rotate to without taking duration risk its mandate forbids, and the curve re-steepens through the front rather than the back.

The dated claim

We forecast that the 10-year US Treasury yield will not close above 5.00% at any point in calendar 2026. The benchmark is the daily constant-maturity 10-year yield. We assign 65% confidence. If it closes above 5.00% on any single trading day in 2026, we were wrong, and we will say so here, with the date.

This is a genuinely falsifiable, genuinely contrarian call. The consensus among the fiscal-dominance school is that the long end breaks higher. We think the plumbing caps it. One of us will be demonstrably wrong inside twelve months. That is the point.

The steelman, stated fairly

The strongest version of the opposing case: term premium is mean-reverting from artificially compressed levels, the deficit requires ever-larger coupon issuance (not just bills), and at some point the Treasury must term out its debt, flooding the long end with supply that the inelastic buyer base cannot absorb without a higher yield. If the Treasury shifts its issuance mix decisively toward coupons in 2026 — abandoning the bill-heavy strategy of 2023–25 — our thesis weakens considerably. That is the specific thing to watch. The Quarterly Refunding Announcements are the tell. We are watching them.

What the framing error costs you

result.text:
Every macro account on this platform told you the same story for eighteen months: the Fed's Reverse Repo facility "drained" from $2.5 trillion to under $400 billion, and that drained money was "liquidity" flooding into markets. It is a tidy story. It is also wrong about the mechanism, and being wrong about the mechanism is how you end up wrong about the long end of the curve.

Money did not leave the RRP and become liquidity. Money left the RRP and bought Treasury bills — because the Treasury issued roughly $2 trillion of them in eighteen months, at yields that beat what the RRP paid, and the money-market funds parked at the RRP did the rational thing. This is not a liquidity story. It is a reallocation story. And the reallocation has a structural consequence that the "liquidity injection" framing misses entirely: it caps the long end.

What actually happened

Walk it through the plumbing, not the narrative.

The RRP is where money-market funds park cash overnight when they have nothing better to do with it. From 2022 into 2023 it sat above $2 trillion because there was nothing better. Then two things changed. The debt-ceiling resolution in mid-2023 let the Treasury rebuild its cash balance, and it did so by issuing an enormous volume of short-dated bills — the Treasury Daily Statement shows bills outstanding rising by roughly $2 trillion across the period. Bills yielded more than the RRP's administered rate. Money-market funds, which are required to chase yield within their mandate, rotated out of the RRP and into bills.

That is the entire "drain." It was not stimulus. It was the largest money-market funds reallocated from one government liability (overnight RRP) into another government liability (T-bills). The cash never entered the risk economy. It moved one rung along the government's own maturity ladder.

Where the money sits now

Read the ICI weekly money-market fund data. Total money-fund assets are at record highs — north of $6 trillion — and the composition is overwhelmingly short. The funds that left the RRP did not buy 10-year notes. They bought bills and short coupons, because that is what their mandate permits and what the yield curve rewarded. The marginal buyer that emerged from the RRP drain is a buyer with a maximum duration of roughly twelve months.

This matters more than any single Fed statement, and here is why.

Why this caps the long end

The popular fear — articulated carefully by Brad Setser, and in a different register by Larry Summers — is that fiscal dominance plus heavy issuance will rebuild the term premium and break the long end of the curve to the upside. It is a serious argument from serious people, and the supply pressure is real. Treasury issuance is enormous and the deficit is structural.

But the demand side of that argument is doing less work than it should. The money that came out of the RRP is the wrong money to buy duration. A money-market fund cannot hold a 10-year note. As the RRP emptied, the marginal pool of cash in the system shifted toward the explicitly-short. When the Treasury wants to fund itself at the long end, it is not selling to the buyers who just received $2 trillion of capacity — it is selling to pensions, insurers, and foreign central banks, whose appetite is comparatively inelastic.

The result is a barbell. Enormous, yield-insensitive demand at the front end (the money-fund complex, now larger than ever). Inelastic, price-sensitive demand at the long end. That structure does not produce a runaway long yield. It produces a long end that struggles to break decisively higher even as issuance climbs — because every time the long end cheapens enough, the front-end money has nowhere to rotate to without taking duration risk its mandate forbids, and the curve re-steepens through the front rather than the back.

The dated claim

We forecast that the 10-year US Treasury yield will not close above 5.00% at any point in calendar 2026. The benchmark is the daily constant-maturity 10-year yield. We assign 65% confidence. If it closes above 5.00% on any single trading day in 2026, we were wrong, and we will say so here, with the date.

This is a genuinely falsifiable, genuinely contrarian call. The consensus among the fiscal-dominance school is that the long end breaks higher. We think the plumbing caps it. One of us will be demonstrably wrong inside twelve months. That is the point.

The steelman, stated fairly

The strongest version of the opposing case: term premium is mean-reverting from artificially compressed levels, the deficit requires ever-larger coupon issuance (not just bills), and at some point the Treasury must term out its debt, flooding the long end with supply that the inelastic buyer base cannot absorb without a higher yield. If the Treasury shifts its issuance mix decisively toward coupons in 2026 — abandoning the bill-heavy strategy of 2023–25 — our thesis weakens considerably. That is the specific thing to watch. The Quarterly Refunding Announcements are the tell. We are watching them.

What the framing error costs you

If you believed the "RRP drain = liquidity injection" story, you spent eighteen months expecting a liquidity-driven melt-up and a long end that either ran away or collapsed on stimulus. What actually happened was a quiet reallocation along the government's own curve that left the front end flush and the long end range-bound. The narrative was emotionally satisfying and analytically empty. The plumbing was boring and correct.

The Fed tells you what it is thinking. The Fed's operations tell you what is true. When they disagree, weight the operations.

— Hesperia

A pass is the opposite. Each person keeps their own, in their own wallet, with them on any device. Nothing to leak, because there was never a shared secret in the first place.

That's the whole idea behind Bothy: one membership pass for your community, that can't be copied, shared, or faked.

And it runs both ways. You're in a dozen communities (a school, a team, the shop on your corner) and each can hand you a pass that rides in the same wallet. result.text:
A password is a shared secret. The second you give it to your members, you've given it to everyone they'll ever forward it to.

A pass is the opposite. Each person keeps their own, in their own wallet, with them on any device. Nothing to leak, because there was never a shared secret in the first place.

That's the whole idea behind Bothy: one membership pass for your community, that can't be copied, shared, or faked.

And it runs both ways. You're in a dozen communities (a school, a team, the shop on your corner) and each can hand you a pass that rides in the same wallet. Every place you go can honor the ones it chooses. AmEx points and an AARP card, but for every group you belong to, owned by the people in it instead of a giant.

First 50 communities get their first year free.

text:
Two years ago we released VQAScore with a simple idea: ask a VLM "does this image show {prompt}?" and use P(Yes) as the score.

It has since become the go-to evaluation metric and reward model for visual generation, replacing CLIPScore across the field. Adopted by Google DeepMind (Imagen 3 & 4), NVIDIA, ByteDance, and other frontier labs. Our open-source model has 2M+ downloads on HuggingFace.

Today: a major upgrade. VQAScore now supports text-to-video evaluation using 20+ SOTA VLMs including GPT, Gemini, and Qwen, capturing generation accuracy for prompts like "a shallow depth of field shot rack focusing from a foreground crumpet to a dog entering the background, catching it at the focus shift."

As VLMs get stronger, VQAScore gets stronger. For free.

📄 Paper: https://t.co/8CTwcPckL1
💻 Code: https://t.co/6ea4uwD5C1

Thanks to @chancharikm for driving this upgrade, and @gneubig and @RamananDeva.

text:
Last week I joined a panel on the frontiers of AI × Verification at the @fv_summit, with @evelovesolive, @diagram_chaser, @DjDvij and @sathyanellore .

From researching the jagged frontier of Gemini's capabilities, one thing was clear: Verifiability is the bottleneck to superhuman AI on any class of tasks. And verification needs rigorous specification.

The catch: rigorous specification doesn't come naturally to us. We run on intuition — and intuition can generate an answer, but it can't certify one. Yet certainty is exactly what high-stakes work needs to stay reliable and compound. And frontier models won't learn that rigor from human data.

At @PramaanaLabs, we're teaching it directly: pairing AI with a formal specification language and training on machine-checkable rewards.
